references.text: When many of Jesus' disciples withdrew, Peter and the twelve confirmed their loyalty and stayed with him. This shows that they had 'endured' with Jesus, as he acknowledges in John 6:67-69.

In the parable of the sower, Jesus describes those who endure through trials – unlike those who fall away at the time of temptation (Luke 8:13-15). The disciples' perseverance with Jesus through his trials is a fulfillment of this ideal.
Jesus himself was tested and tempted, and Hebrews 2:18 confirms that he suffered through temptations. The disciples were with him through these trials (πειρασμοῖς).

Jesus says that the disciples are to bear witness about him because they have been with him from the beginning (John 15:27). This underscores the same point: the disciples had faithfully followed him throughout his entire ministry.

Peter describes the qualification for being an apostle as having accompanied Jesus throughout his entire public ministry – from John's baptism to the ascension (Acts 1:21-22). This confirms that they had endured with Jesus.

Shortly after this statement, Jesus exhorts the disciples to pray not to enter into temptation (Luke 22:40), which shows the ongoing struggle with πειρασμός (trials/temptations) as the context for Jesus' words.

After the temptation in the wilderness, the devil left Jesus 'until an opportune time' (Luke 4:13). Jesus' 'trials' (πειρασμοῖς) encompassed his entire ministry, and the disciples were with him through them.

Paul writes that if we endure, we will also reign with Christ (2 Timothy 2:12). This reflects the connection in Luke 22:28-30, where Jesus links the disciples' perseverance to the promise of reigning with him in his kingdom.

Jesus promises the church in Philadelphia protection because they have held fast to his word about endurance (Revelation 3:10). The theme of enduring trials and receiving reward is the same as in Jesus' words to the disciples.
